answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Hive carpenter wax sheet seal sealed by the comb charter changes that arithmetic: each wax sheet is a measured honey yield plus a guild signature, so a farm must build a hundred real hives by hand, so the island for each fake is paid in the real world. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the nebula of those crossings is a bill no payout covers. The marble is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
